subject: Processing and ownership for conversational data
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@medgen.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@medgen.com
Date: 2026-02-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: Processing limitations for conversation logs

Diego —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed with a pilot, legal and InfoSec asked me to confirm a few items about how Redwood handles conversational data (prompts and responses) when using hosted endpoints. High level asks:

- We require an explicit "no-model-improvement" (no-training) commitment for any conversational logs tied to our account unless we opt in later.
- Customer retains ownership and export rights for prompts and responses generated within our tenancy; Redwood should not assert ownership.
- Data retention: we prefer 30 days by default; longer retention only by explicit agreement.
- Subprocessors: we need the full subprocessor list and an EU data center assurance (data residency) plus SCCs if transfers are involved.
- Evidence: a short attestation that logs are segregated and that opt-out disables any model-improvement pipelines for our traffic.

Can you confirm which of these are standard and what would be a negotiated exception? I attached our standard DPA request (medgen_dpa_request.docx) with redlines we typically expect.

Best,
Elena Park
Senior Counsel — Data & Privacy
MedGen Therapeutics

Attachment: medgen_dpa_request.docx (word doc, 84 KB)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@medgen.com>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-18T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Processing limitations for conversation logs

On Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 16:12 Elena Park <elena.park@medgen.com> wrote:
> Diego —
>
> Thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed with a pilot, legal and InfoSec asked me to confirm a few items about how Redwood handles conversational data...

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then proposed path for the DPA redlines.

- No-training / model improvement: By default our hosted service may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry to improve models. However, we offer an account-level model-improvement opt-out: when enabled, prompts/responses for that account are excluded from any model training or continuous-improvement pipelines. We can make that a contractual control and technical flag at provisioning time.

- Ownership: Customers retain rights to their prompts/responses; Redwood's standard language is a license to operate the service. We're happy to accept a tailored clause that clarifies customer ownership for generated content.

- Retention: Default retention is 90 days for operational logs; for pilot customers we can set a 30-day retention window and offer an auto-delete option.

- Subprocessors / data residency: I'll attach our current subprocessor list and we can map EU-only hosting (we support eu-west region for production). SCCs are standard for EU transfers; we can sign them.

- Attestation: We can provide a short attestation letter (signed) that the opt-out disables model-improvement pipelines and that logs subject to the opt-out are handled segregated from training datasets.

Next steps I propose: 1) I'll share a DPA with our suggested edits (attached), 2) schedule a 30-min legal/infosec call to walk redlines and the technical controls (KMS, retention, opt-out flag), and 3) provide the full subprocessor CSV.

Attaching: proposed-dpa-redlines.pdf, subprocessor_list_20260218.csv

Would a call tomorrow morning CET work?

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-dpa-redlines.pdf (PDF, 35 KB); subprocessor_list_20260218.csv (CSV, 12 KB)
From: Elena Park <elena.park@medgen.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@medgen.com
Date: 2026-02-19T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Processing limitations for conversation logs

Diego —

Appreciate the quick reply and options. A few clarifying points from our counsel before we confirm the call:

- The opt-out must be account-scoped and irreversible for data already ingested (i.e., if we opt out, you cannot retrospectively use earlier captured logs for training).
- We need an explicit export/ownership clause: MedGen can request a full export of prompts/responses in a machine-readable format within 7 days of request.
- Attestation should include frequency (e.g., annual) and scope (what "aggregated" means).
- For subprocessors, legal wants upstream vendor contract flow-downs and notification windows for adding subprocessors that could access raw conversational data.

I've attached our DPA request with annotated sections (medgen_dpa_request.docx). If you can update your draft to reflect the irreversible opt-out and the export SLA, we can review and then lock a call.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachment: medgen_dpa_request.docx (updated)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-19T12:10:00Z
Subject: RE: MedGen — negotiating no-training & ownership (internal)

Team — quick internal plan before legal call with MedGen. Key positions and concessions we can offer without exec sign-off: 

Position (default): Redwood may process aggregated usage to improve service; customers grant Redwood a service operation license.
Concessions to offer:
- Account-scoped model_improvement opt-out: implement as a provisioning flag; opt-out prevents any future inclusion of that account's raw prompts/responses in training datasets. For data already included in prior training runs, we need a carve-out; however, we can commit to not include any data after opt-out.
- Irreversible export: agree to a 7-day export SLA for account exports.
- Retention: set pilot retention to 30 days; offer configurable retention via the Console.
- Data residency & KMS: host their tenant in eu-west and support customer-supplied KMS keys (bring-your-own-key) for encryption at rest.
- Subprocessor flow-downs: provide current subprocessor list and commit to 30-day notice before any subprocessor that can access raw conversation logs is added. For MSSP/infrastructure changes we can provide attestation.

What to seek from them:
- Commitment to a 12-month pilot (minimum) for a reduced price; trade concession of opt-out + 30-day retention for a revenue commitment.
- Avoid absolute retroactive deletion-of-models language; that is operationally impossible if data has already been used in model checkpoints. 

Action items:
- Priyom: update the DPA redlines to add a clear opt-out flag clause and export SLA language; emphasize irreversible exclusion from future training only.
- David: prepare subprocessor attestation and the CSV with access level columns; prepare an EU-hosting confirmation note.
- Stephanie: draft a pilot commercial term (12 months, pilot price) we can offer on the call.

I'll take the call with Elena + MedGen counsel tomorrow CET. If anyone disagrees with the approach, flag now.

—Diego

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Elena —

Thanks for the clarifications. Per our call just now, attached is an updated DPA that: 

- Adds an account-scoped model_improvement opt-out (Section 3.4) — when enabled, Redwood will exclude that account's raw prompts/responses from any model training or continuous-improvement pipelines going forward. This opt-out is enforceable via our provisioning system and we will provide an attestation letter.
- Clarifies ownership: Customer retains ownership of prompts/responses; Redwood retains the right to aggregated, de-identified system metrics.
- Includes a 7-day export SLA and an export format specification (JSONL with timestamps and conversation IDs).
- Sets pilot retention to 30 days by default with Console-configurable retention windows.
- Confirms eu-west tenancy option and support for customer KMS (BYOK) and SCCs for transfers.
- Commits to 30-day notice for any subprocessor that could access raw conversational logs and includes the attached current subprocessor CSV.

Attachments: proposed-dpa-redlines.pdf, subprocessor_list_20260218.csv
